lines.japanese: えーと、まー、どーでもいいことなんですけどー。
lines.english: Umm, well, this is totally unimportant, but...

lines.japanese: 色褪せない名曲、なーんて表現があるじゃないですか。でも逆に、色褪せているからこそ意味があるっていう音楽もあると思うんですよね。
lines.english: You know how people say a classic never fades? Well, I think some music means something precisely because it has faded.

lines.japanese: たとえば一例としてですけど。えー、さかのぼること十数年前、わが国におけるお茶の間的シーンにおいて、歌謡曲からニューミュージックへの過渡期に生まれた時代の寵児とも言える楽曲群があります。
lines.english: Take one example. A little over a decade ago, when the music in Japan’s living rooms was shifting from old-school pop to the singer-songwriter sound they called New Music, a whole crop of songs appeared—darlings of their age, you might say.

lines.japanese: ジャンル的にはアイドルポップなんて言うんですかね。まあ、これが世間の音楽通からは軽視されてると言いますか、同じ音楽というカテゴリーにすら組みこませてもらっていないフシがありますけども。
lines.english: Genre-wise, I guess you'd call it idol pop. And, well, people who really know music tend to look down on it. Sometimes it feels like they won't even let it into the same category as music at all.

lines.japanese: ええまあ、たしかにアイドルソングっていうのは、当時からしてすでにショウビジネスのもっともエグい一面でして。百人の玄人に顔をしかめられようと、千人の素人に金を出させればええんじゃいな世界ですよね。
lines.english: Sure, idol songs already showed off the nastiest side of show business even back then. Who cares if a hundred pros turn up their noses, as long as a thousand regular people cough up the cash, right?

lines.japanese: そもそもコマーシャルな素材としてたまたま音楽って手段を用いただけですから、アート的な意味での完成度なんて求められてませんし、あからさまに「作品であるより商品たれ」だったんですよ。
lines.english: I mean, music just happened to be the medium they used for something commercial. Nobody was asking for artistic perfection, and the message was pretty blatant: be a product before you're a work of art.

lines.japanese: でもね、ほら。そこまで貪欲に商業主義を前面に出しちゃってる曲がヒットチャートを独占したり大量生産されたりっていうのは、あの時代ならではの風潮でしょ。
lines.english: But look, songs that shoved commercialism that greedily right in your face could take over the charts and get churned out by the truckload. That was very much a thing of that era, right?

lines.japanese: 現在だったらもっと上手いこと「作品」に昇華して見せたげないと、なかなかランキングの上位は取れないですよね。ましてやチャートにずらり並んだりなんて、とてもとても。
lines.english: These days, if you don't do a better job dressing it up as a 'work of art,' it's pretty hard to rank near the top, right? Never mind filling the whole chart. No way.

lines.japanese: そんなアイドルポップ華やかなりし時代、あまたの少年少女たちが彗星のごとく現れては消えていったわけですが、えー、その中でもっとも知られているのが伝説の５人組『フリッキー５』ではないでしょうか。
lines.english: So back in idol pop's glory days, all kinds of boys and girls appeared and vanished like comets. Um, and the best-known of them has to be the legendary five-member group Fricky Five, right?

lines.japanese: とくに国内シングルチャート１２週連続１位という偉業を成しとげた大ヒットナンバー『ほほえみジェノサイド』は、老若男女を問わず日本列島を熱狂の渦に巻きこんだものです。
lines.english: Their colossal hit “Smiling Genocide,” which held the number-one position on the domestic singles chart for twelve consecutive weeks, swept the Japanese archipelago into a frenzy that spared neither young nor old, man nor woman.

lines.japanese: まだ四隅が丸かったころの画面の中で、彼らはステージ上に立ちこめた乳白色のミルキーウェイを切り、ピーターパンのように滑走していました。
lines.english: On television screens whose corners were still rounded, they parted the milky-white Milky Way of stage fog and glided across it like Peter Pan.

lines.japanese: ビブラートもヒーカップもどこ吹く風、あくまで自然体で歌いあげるナチュラルなスタイルは若さと瑞々しさに溢れていて、いっそ清々しいとさえ言えましょう。
lines.english: Vibrato? Vocal hiccups? Who needed them? Their perfectly natural singing brimmed with youth and freshness. You might even call it bracing.

lines.japanese: 歌は技術でなく心で歌うもの──だとすれば、パワーまかせのヴォーカルはティーンならではの爽快な情熱をプレーンなままに出力しており、聴く者のハートになにか勇気にも似たものを湧出させます。
lines.english: If song is born of the heart rather than technique, their sheer force of voice expressed teenage ardor in its plainest form and made something almost like courage spring up in the listener’s breast.

lines.japanese: いま。いまだからこそ、聞いてもらいたい一曲。あの弾けたイントロが耳に飛びこんでくれば、銀色のきらびやかなステージ衣装をまとったフリファと共に、オーディエンスそれぞれの青春もまた甦るはず。
lines.english: Now. Now, precisely, is when I want you to hear it. The moment that explosive introduction bursts into your ears, your own youth will rise again beside the Frickies in their glittering silver costumes.

lines.japanese: 彼らの楽曲は、色褪せているからこそに美しい──そうです。伝説の少年たちが本邦音楽史に残した十代の叫びは、すなわち現代のミュージックシーンに欠けているなにかでもあるのです。
lines.english: Their music is beautiful because it has faded. Yes: the teenage cry those legendary boys left in the history of Japanese music is also something absent from the music scene of today.

lines.japanese: いやあ、アイドルって本当にいいものですね。
lines.english: Ahh, idols really are wonderful things.

lines.japanese: 米田編集の眼球が追っていたのは、非情なことにそのあたりの行まででした。
lines.english: Unfortunately, that was as far as Editor Yoneda's eyes had traveled.

lines.japanese: 「はーい、それじゃー玉稿いただきましたー」
lines.english: Okaaay, your esteemed manuscript is officially receiiived.
“What?!”

lines.japanese: 彼女がその原稿用紙五枚を早々と山折りして息つくように顔を上げるものですから、俺は思わず首から上を前に突きだすオーバーリアクションを披露してしまいました。
lines.english: She promptly folded the five manuscript pages into a little ridge and looked up as though surfacing for air. I reacted by jerking my head and neck toward her in extravagant disbelief.

lines.japanese: 「え、もう読んだんすか？　読んでないすよね？　読めないほどひどいんすか！　ひどいんすか俺！」
lines.english: “You’ve read it already? You haven’t, have you? Is it so terrible you can’t read it? Am I terrible?”

lines.japanese: 「違う違う、君を信頼してるからだってば」
lines.english: “No, no. It means I trust you.”

lines.japanese: 「信頼……ああそう、それ！　信頼！　うん、信頼してるからこそ、もういいかなって」
lines.english: “Trust... yes, that’s it! Trust! Precisely because I trust you, I think that’ll do.”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは右手をひらひらさせてソッポ向きながら、なんとも嘘くさい言葉をあさっての方向へ発射しました。
lines.english: Waving her right hand and looking away, Yoneda fired those deeply implausible words in entirely the wrong direction.

lines.japanese: 「いんすか！　いんすか、そんなんで！　いくらモノクロページの隅っこコラムだからって！　いくらアルバイトの素人に書かせた、誌面稼ぎのやっつけ仕事だからって！」
lines.english: “That’s enough? Really? Even if it’s only a little column tucked into the corner of a black-and-white page! Even if it’s slapdash filler assigned to a part-time amateur just to eat up space!”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　もう千歳君、自虐的だなあ。図々しいぐらいの自信がなきゃ、バイトとは言えこういう仕事やってけないよ」
lines.english: Huh? Come on, Chitose, you're way too hard on yourself. Even if it's only part-time, you need enough confidence to be almost shameless if you wanna survive this kind of work.

lines.japanese: 「俺に自信がないなら、米田さんには愛がないですよ！　担当さんとしての愛がなさすぎですよ！」
lines.english: “If I lack confidence, you lack love! You show far too little love as my editor!”

lines.japanese: 「だーいじょぶ、だってば。愛を込めて校正屋さんに回しとくから」
lines.english: “It’s fine, honestly. I’ll send it to the proofreader with all my love.”

lines.japanese: 「ひとまかせの愛！？」
lines.english: “Love delegated to a third party?!”

lines.japanese: しかし俺の抗議もむなしく、米田さんは原稿用紙をＡ４封筒に入れると、その表面にでかでかと黒マジックで『懐レビュ』『１月売り』と殴り書きして、散らかったデスクの端に寄せました。
lines.english: My protests availed me nothing. Yoneda slipped the manuscript into an A4 envelope, scrawled RETRO REVIEW and JANUARY ON-SALE across it in thick black marker, and pushed it to the edge of her cluttered desk.

lines.japanese: 「ええー、米田さぁーん。だって校正さんが見てくれるのは文字的なミスだけでしょー。文章の内容とかはチェックしなくていいんすかー」
lines.english: Come ooon, Yonedaaa. The proofreader only looks for typos and stuff, right? Don't you need to check what the article actually says?

lines.japanese: 「んー、分かったよ……じゃあ、あとで読んどくから」
lines.english: “Fine, fine... I’ll read it later.”

lines.japanese: 「『じゃああとで』ってアナタ！　そんな、夏休みの宿題をいなす７月下旬の小学生みたいに！」
lines.english: “‘Fine, later’? You sound like a grade-schooler fending off summer homework at the end of July!”

lines.japanese: 「だって私、ここんとこ睡眠不足が続いててさぁ。働く大人はつらいわぁ……」
lines.english: Because I've been running on no sleep latelyyy. Being a working adult is rough...

lines.japanese: そんなことを言いながら、しょぼしょぼと子供みたいに目をこする米田さん。
lines.english: As she spoke, Yoneda rubbed her bleary eyes like a child.

lines.japanese: 「テンパってるときに千歳君の原稿読んでると、こっちまで洗脳されそうになっちゃうんだよねー」
lines.english: When I'm freaking out and I read your copy, Chitose, I start feeling like I'm getting brainwashed toooo.

lines.japanese: 「は、なんすか洗脳って」
lines.english: “What do you mean, brainwashed?”

lines.japanese: 「ほら。千歳君、それらしい御託ならべてなんでもかんでも誉めちぎるじゃない。だからうっかり、あーそうかもなー、これはこれでいいのかもなーとかってさ」
lines.english: See? You pile up all this plausible-sounding stuff and praise absolutely everything, right? Then I let my guard down and start going, ohh, maybe he's right, maybe this is fine after all...

lines.japanese: 「それ洗脳じゃないっすよ！　啓蒙っすよ！」
lines.english: “That isn’t brainwashing! It’s enlightenment!”

lines.japanese: 「ていうか、ほんと、フリッキー５はイイっすよ？　アリっすよ？　捨てたもんじゃないっすよ？」
lines.english: No, but seriously, Fricky Five are good, okay? They're legit, okay? They're not half bad, okay?

lines.japanese: 「はいはい、あとで読むからいいってば……まあ、うら若き乙女のころは私も人並にハマったけどさ」
lines.english: “Yes, yes, I’ll read it later. I admit that when I was a tender young maiden, I fell for them as hard as anyone.”

lines.japanese: 「え、誰のファンだったんすか？　やっぱホソリュー？　それとも渋いとこ突いてマサシとか？」
lines.english: Huh, who were you a fan of? Hosoryu, obviously? Or did you go obscure and pick Masashi?

lines.japanese: 「うあー、やめてやめて。数々の若気のいたりが甦る」
lines.english: “Ugh, stop. You’re resurrecting all the sins of my youth.”

lines.japanese: 「甦らせてくださいよぅ。フリッキー５は時空を越えるレジェンドっすよ。いっそ巻頭特集でどどんと一発やりましょうよ、フリファ・メモリアルとかって」
lines.english: “Let them rise again! The Fricky Five are legends who transcend space and time. Let's give them a huge lead feature—Frickies Memorial!”

lines.japanese: 「しつこいなー。キミ、フリーター辞めてうちの営業部入ったら？」
lines.english: “You never give up. Why don't you quit being a part-timer and join our sales department?”

lines.japanese: 「一流企業に縁故採用！？　マジっすか、入ります入ります、紹介状ください紹介状」
lines.english: “A job at a first-rate corporation through personal connections?! Seriously? I’m in! Write me a letter of introduction!”

lines.japanese: 「ヒラの私になに期待するかな、この子は。だいたいさ、千歳君まだ就職する気なんてないんでしょ？　いいよねえ青い春って。手探りの季節だァ、可能性の塊だァ」
lines.english: “What do you expect from a rank-and-file employee? Besides, you still have no intention of getting a proper job, do you? Ah, springtime of youth. The season of fumbling your way forward. A solid mass of possibility.”

lines.japanese: 「痛っ、痛っ！　オフィス・レディの疲弊した眼光がプーの柔肌にひしひし痛いっす！」
lines.english: “Ow, ow! That exhausted career-woman glare is biting painfully into the soft skin of this bum!”

lines.japanese: とかっておどけてはみせても、やっぱり十も離れてない米田さんにまるでモラトリアム世代の象徴みたいな目で見られると、なんだか申しわけない気分になってきます。
lines.english: I could joke around like that, but when Yoneda—not even ten years older than me—looked at me like I was the poster boy for prolonged adolescence, I started to feel kind of bad.

lines.japanese: 一流大学をストレートで出てそのまま大手出版社に入ったという米田さんは、体を俺に向けたままで、ちらりとパソコンのディスプレイを確認しました。
lines.english: She had graduated from an elite university on schedule and gone straight into a major publishing house. Still turned toward me, she flicked a glance at her computer monitor.

lines.japanese: 「んー、やっぱ違うかな……」
lines.english: “Hmm. No, that’s not quite right...”

lines.japanese: そして、小さな声でつぶやいてからマウスに手を伸ばしました。
lines.english: She murmured under her breath and reached for the mouse.

lines.japanese: 「旋回やり過ぎたか……端だけバンクさせて……うーん、いっそここは原形とどめないぐらいに……」
lines.english: “Too much rotation... tilt just the edge... Hmm. Maybe I should distort this until the original is unrecognizable...”

lines.japanese: 米田さんの右手の下からカチカチ音がするたびに、画面の中の見出し文字がうねったり尖ったりその表情を変えていきます。
lines.english: Each click beneath her right hand made the headline on the screen writhe, sharpen, and assume a different expression.
“Oh? Oh?”

lines.japanese: 指一本で出来るマジック。同じ文字列でもほんの少しの加工でいろんな印象になるものです。
lines.english: Magic you can do with one finger. Even the exact same words can feel totally different with just a tiny change.

lines.japanese: 「はー。なんか便利っすねえ、こんぴーたー」
lines.english: “Wow. These com-pu-tor contraptions certainly are convenient.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　ああ……」
lines.english: “What? Oh...”

lines.japanese: 米田さんはいまどき珍しい日本語に遭遇したかのような目で、ぼけーっと突っ立っていた俺の姿を見上げました。
lines.english: Yoneda looked up at me, standing there in a daze, as if she had encountered an unusually archaic Japanese expression.

lines.japanese: 「うん、便利っていうかもう必需品だよね。いまだいぶ安くなってきてるし、千歳君も早く揃えた方がいいよ。そうすれば私ももっと仕事振れるし」
lines.english: “Yeah, they’re not just convenient—they’re pretty much essential now. They’ve gotten a lot cheaper, too, so you should get yourself set up soon. Then I can send more work your way.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、でもその前に、キミには携帯電話を持ってほしいんだけど──」
lines.english: “Though before that, I wish you would buy a cell phone—”

lines.japanese: 「──っと！　ちょっと待って、内線だ」
lines.english: “—wait. That’s the internal line.”

lines.japanese: 林檎マークの箱型機械の横で、クリーム色の電話機がプルプル鳴りだしました。米田さんは俺にてのひらを向けながら、もう片方の手で受話器を取りあげます。
lines.english: Beside the boxy machine bearing an apple logo, a cream-colored telephone began to trill. Yoneda raised one palm to me and picked up the receiver with her other hand.

lines.japanese: 「へい米田っす……はい……あー、はいどーも、替わりますー」
lines.english: “Yo, Yoneda here... Yes... Ah, hello. Put them through.”

lines.japanese: 「もしもし！　ハイっ、ご無沙汰しておりますヨネダです！　いえっ、こちらこそお世話になっております」
lines.english: “Hello! Yes! Yoneda speaking—it's been far too long! No, no, thank you for all your help.”

lines.japanese: ひと懐っこい声で応対しながら、米田編集は無意識なのかその場でぺこぺこ頭を下げはじめました。
lines.english: Answering in her most personable voice, Yoneda began bowing over and over where she sat, perhaps without even realizing it.

lines.japanese: ふと周りを見れば、メンズフリーズ編集部は入稿日が近いのか、皆さん忙しなく動きまわったり一心にキーボードを叩いたりしていました。
lines.english: Looking around, I saw that a deadline must be near. Everyone in the Men’s Freeze editorial office was hurrying to and fro or hammering intently at a keyboard.

lines.japanese: 電話の声やＯＡ機器の音が雑然としたオフィスに満ちていて、ある種の緊迫した空気が漂っています。
lines.english: Voices on telephones and the sounds of office machinery filled the disorderly room. A certain tension hung in the air.

lines.japanese: 隣りの机で探しものをしている男性編集者の苛立たしさが、なんだか無職の俺に帰れと言ってるように思えてきました。
lines.english: The guy at the next desk was getting irritated as he searched for something, and somehow it started to feel like he was telling unemployed old me to go home.

lines.japanese: あー、なんか居づらい空気。苦手だなあ、こういうの……。
lines.english: Ahh, this is getting awkward. I hate this kind of thing...

lines.japanese: 「ごめんごめん。えーと、なんの話だったっけ？」
lines.english: Sorry, sorry. Um, what were we talking about again?

lines.japanese: 一歩あとずさりかけたところで、受話器を置いた米田さんが、椅子を回して俺に向きなおりました。
lines.english: I was just starting to take a step back when Yoneda hung up the phone, spun her chair around, and faced me again.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうそう！　千歳君にもっと仕事頼みたいって話だ。どう、いまちょうど一本あるんだけど、引きうけてくれない？」
lines.english: Oh, right! I was talking about giving you more work. So, how about it? I've got one right now—wanna take it?

lines.japanese: 「は。マジっすか」
lines.english: “What? Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 居心地の悪さになんとなく背中が丸くなってきた俺ですが、仕事の話となれば堂々と胸を張れます。
lines.english: The awkwardness had me hunching in on myself, but the second work came up, I could puff my chest right back out.

lines.japanese: 「うん。それでお金貯めて、早くケータイ買ってね」
lines.english: “Yes. Save up the money and buy a cell phone soon.”

lines.japanese: 「で、で、どんなお仕事なんすか」
lines.english: “So, so—what sort of job is it?”

lines.japanese: 俺は話を逸らして詰めよりました。
lines.english: I changed the subject and leaned in.

lines.japanese: 「えーと、ちょっと待ってね……」
lines.english: Umm, hang on a sec...

lines.japanese: 米田さんは事務机に積もった書類や資料の山に手を突っこみ、その中から一冊のハードカバーを引きぬきました。
lines.english: Yoneda shoved a hand into the mountain of documents and reference materials piled on her desk and pulled out a hardcover book.

lines.japanese: 「とりあえず、これあげる。ちょっと前に下が出したものなんだけど」
lines.english: “Here. You can keep this. One of the departments downstairs put it out a little while ago.”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは本を持っていない方の手で床を指差しました。たしか下のフロアには文芸誌や一般書籍の編集部なんかがあったはずです。
lines.english: She pointed at the floor with the hand that wasn't holding the book. I was pretty sure there were editorial departments for literary magazines and general books on the floors below.

lines.japanese: 「どうかな。来月頭ぐらいまでに、これの紹介文５０００文字。かなりユルめの文体で」
lines.english: How about this? Five thousand characters introducing it, by around the start of next month. Keep it really loose.

lines.japanese: 俺は首を大袈裟に傾けて、米田さんの持っている本を横から覗きこみました。そして、それほど厚くないことだけ確認するとその場で即断しました。
lines.english: I tilted my head way too far and peeked sideways at the book in her hand. Once I'd checked that it wasn't all that thick, I decided on the spot.

lines.japanese: 「ようがす。引きうけましょう」
lines.english: “Very good. I'll take it.”

lines.japanese: 「うんうん。また適当に誉めちぎっといて」
lines.english: Yeah, yeah. Just gush about it like you always do.

lines.japanese: 「誉め一丁、喜んで！」
lines.english: “One order of praise, gladly!”

lines.japanese: 米田さんが差しだした本を、俺は卒業証書を受けとるみたいに両手で丁重に受けとりました。
lines.english: I received the book she offered with both hands and all the solemnity of accepting a diploma.

lines.japanese: 「……で、どんな内容なんすかこれ」
lines.english: “...What is it about?”

lines.japanese: 「元ＡＶ嬢の実体験エッセイ集」
lines.english: “A collection of personal essays by a former adult-video actress.”

lines.japanese: 「ぅわお！　服脱ぐ女優が心まで脱ぎました！」
lines.english: “Wow! The actress who bared her body now bares her heart!”

lines.japanese: 「聞いた話だと、基本えっち系なんだけど、ときおり泣きどころもあるらしいよ」
lines.english: “From what I hear, it’s mostly sexy material, but every now and then there’s a part that makes you cry.”

lines.japanese: 「ポロリもあるけどホロリもあるよ！」
lines.english: “A little nip slip and a little tear drip!”

lines.japanese: 「そうそう、そんな感じの馬鹿テキストでお願い」
lines.english: “Exactly. Give me that sort of idiotic copy.”

lines.japanese: 「……いま、馬鹿って言いました？」
lines.english: “...Did you just call it idiotic?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、早い話がコレ、うちの商品の販促だから。いつもの調子で、ベタベタに甘やかしたレビューお願いしますね、千歳先生」
lines.english: Well, long story short, this is just a sales promo for one of our products. So give it one of your usual cloyingly sweet reviews, okay, our distinguished author?

lines.japanese: 「いや、いま馬鹿って言いましたよね？　千歳先生に」
lines.english: “You did call it idiotic, didn’t you? Right to your distinguished author’s face.”

lines.japanese: 「それにしてもカケル遅いねえ。自分から来るって言ったんでしょ？」
lines.english: “Kakeru’s really late. He was the one who said he’d come, right?”

lines.japanese: 「ふんだ、そんな、思いだしたように話題変えたって釣られないやい」
lines.english: Hmph! You can't just change the subject like you suddenly remembered something and expect me to fall for it!

lines.japanese: 「ま、あの子が時間守らないのはいまに始まったことでもないか」
lines.english: Well, Kakeru being late is nothing new.

lines.japanese: 米田さんは椅子をきぃと軋ませて、背もたれに体重を預けました。
lines.english: Yoneda’s chair creaked as she leaned her weight against its back.

lines.japanese: 「ねえ、カケルってさ、昔からああだったの？」
lines.english: “Tell me, has Kakeru always been like that?”

lines.japanese: 「え、話変えるの癪ですけど、なんすか『ああ』って」
lines.english: Hey, I'm still mad you're changing the subject, but what do you mean by 'like that'?

lines.japanese: 「だから、ああいうさ……うーん、マイペースっていうか、自分を貫くっていうか……」
lines.english: “You know... Hmm. Moving at his own pace. Refusing to bend...”

lines.japanese: 「ぶっちゃけて言うと？」
lines.english: “In plain language?”

lines.japanese: 「クソ生意気なガキ」
lines.english: “An obnoxious little brat.”

lines.japanese: 「ねえさん、ぶっちゃけ過ぎ」
lines.english: “Whoa, that’s a little too honest.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、いいんだけどね。私は仕事柄、エキセントリックな人間を相手にするのわりと慣れてるし。あと軽部先輩から紹介された時点で、いきなり『素行に問題あるが長い目で見守ってくれ』なんて言われてたし」
lines.english: “I don't particularly mind. My job has made me fairly accustomed to eccentrics. Besides, when Karube introduced him, the first thing he said was, ‘The boy has conduct problems, but take the long view and watch over him.’”

lines.japanese: 「でも、普通はそう簡単に済まされないでしょ。あんな生き方してて、ねえ、損じゃない」
lines.english: “Still, most people won’t dismiss it so easily. Living the way he does has to cost him, doesn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ほら、あれっすよ。きっと彼、フクザツな生い立ちとかあるんすよ」
lines.english: “Well, you know. I’m sure he has some complicated past.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、グレ方としちゃ中途半端だと思うけどね。はっきり言って大人げないし。構ってほしくて憎まれ口叩いてる子供みたいじゃない？」
lines.english: Hmm, if he's trying to act like a delinquent, he's only halfway there. Honestly, it's pretty childish. Doesn't he just look like a kid saying nasty stuff because he wants attention?

lines.japanese: 「ええまあ。そう見えるからこそ、べつに腹も立たないんすけど」
lines.english: “Yes, perhaps. But that’s exactly why I don’t take offense.”

lines.japanese: 「まあねえ……昔の軽部先輩みたいに、何十人っていうヤンキー集団のアタマ張っちゃうような本気っぽいのも、それはそれでドン引きだけどさ」
lines.english: Yeah... though if he went all-in like Karube used to and became the boss of some delinquent gang with dozens of guys, that'd be seriously off-putting too.

lines.japanese: 「え、うそ！　低俗なお下劣ジョークを飛ばしては日々女性アルバイトにこっぴどく叱られている、あのうだつの上がらない軽部狩男３５歳に、そんな人知れぬバリバリ伝説が！？」
lines.english: Whaaat?! No way! You mean that washed-up, thirty-five-year-old Karuo Karube—the guy who spends every day cracking filthy lowbrow jokes and getting chewed out by the women on staff—has some secret Roaring Legend nobody knows about?!

lines.japanese: 「え、初耳？　うっそ、先輩これ内緒にしてたのかな……あはは、いまの聞かなかったことにしてね」
lines.english: “You hadn’t heard? Oh no, was he keeping that quiet...? Ahaha. Pretend I never said it.”

lines.japanese: 「え、えええ、難しい記憶操作をさらりと要請するなあこのひと」
lines.english: W-w-wait, don't just casually ask me for advanced memory manipulation, lady!

lines.japanese: 「ええと、じゃあ話をカケルに戻そう。千歳君は、彼と長いんだっけ？」
lines.english: “Right, then. Back to Kakeru. Have you known him long?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、初めて会ったのは一年ぐらい前すかね。たしか去年のいま頃だったかな、裸Ｙシャツ喫茶の立て看板を設置するバイトでたまたま同じ組になったんすよ」
lines.english: Hmm, we met about a year ago, I guess. Around this time last year, maybe? We just happened to get paired up on this job putting out signs for a café where the waitresses wore dress shirts with nothing underneath.

lines.japanese: 「なんつーバイトしてんの、キミら」
lines.english: “What kind of jobs do you two take?”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、なに言ってんですか。ジャンル的にはある意味、広告代理業っすよ。つったらリクルートの花形、大学４年生の憧れじゃないすか」
lines.english: No, no, what're you talking about? Genre-wise, that's basically advertising-agency work. And advertising is the star of recruiting season, right? Every fourth-year college student's dream.

lines.japanese: 「で？　夜中にあちこちまわって？　電柱にタテカンくくりつけてるうちに意気投合して？」
lines.english: “So you traveled around at night, tying signs to utility poles, and gradually bonded?”

lines.japanese: 「や、そうでもなかったすよ。俺はぺらぺら喋ってたけど、彼はむっつり黙ってたし。むしろウザがられてたんじゃないかなあ」
lines.english: “Nah, not really. I talked my head off, but he sat there in sullen silence. If anything, he probably found me annoying.”

lines.japanese: 「だよねえ。あの子、そんな人なつっこくないもんねえ」
lines.english: “That sounds more like him. He isn’t exactly friendly.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、まあ。ただ、そんときカケルくんが何気に教えてくれた洋食屋があって、試しに行ってみたらいいカンジだったんです」
lines.english: “True. But he casually told me about a Western-style restaurant, and when I tried it, I liked the place.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、それがアレキサンダー？」
lines.english: “Alexander?”

lines.japanese: 「そです。ほいで、通ってるうちに何度か遭遇して」
lines.english: “Right. And once I became a regular, I ran into him there a few times.”

lines.japanese: 「で、自然と意気投合してった、ってわけだ」
lines.english: And then you two naturally hit it off. That's how it goes, right?

lines.japanese: 「や、べつに」
lines.english: “Nah, not really.”

lines.japanese: 「え、じゃいつ意気投合すんの？」
lines.english: Huh? Then when do you two hit it off?

lines.japanese: 「え、この話は意気投合オチにしなきゃいけないんですか」
lines.english: “Wait, does this story have to end on an ‘and that's how we hit it off’ punchline?”

lines.japanese: 「私、若さゆえに不器用な男同士が握手する瞬間って好きなのよねー」
lines.english: I just love that moment when two young guys, all awkward because they're young, finally shake hands, y'know?

lines.japanese: 「はあ。そいじゃ近日中に意気投合しときます」
lines.english: Uh-huh. Well then, we'll make sure to hit it off sometime soon.

lines.japanese: 「えっ、キミら、まだしてなかったの？」
lines.english: “What? You two still haven’t done it?”

lines.japanese: 「ねえさん、その言い方なんか薔薇色」
lines.english: “Whoa, now you’re making it sound like a romance.”

lines.japanese: 「カケルってさ、好きな子とかいないのかな」
lines.english: So, does Kakeru have a girl he likes or anything?

lines.japanese: 「え、ちょっと、この流れでコイバナに持ってくんすか。べつにうちら、薔薇色の関係ないすよ」
lines.english: “Wait, you’re turning this into romantic gossip after that? There’s nothing romantic going on between us.”

lines.japanese: 「そうじゃなくてさ、あいつも真面目に恋愛なんかすれば角が取れて丸くなるんじゃないかなーって」
lines.english: “That isn’t what I mean. I thought a serious relationship might sand down some of his corners.”

lines.japanese: 「……ん？　それとも？　真面目な恋に破れてトゲが出たとか？」
lines.english: “...Unless a serious love ended badly and gave him all those thorns?”

lines.japanese: 「やー、なんにしても、あの圭角の多さと言うか、切れ味鋭いエッジこそがカケルくんの持ち味じゃないかと思いますが」
lines.english: “No, whichever way you look at it, I think all those sharp corners—that keen, cutting edge—are precisely what make Kakeru who he is.”

lines.japanese: 「鋭すぎでしょ。千歳君、カケルのスレッドとか見たことある？」
lines.english: Whoa, way too perceptive. Chitose, have you ever seen the threads about Kakeru?

lines.japanese: 「え、なんすかそれ」
lines.english: “What are those?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうか……パソコン持ってないのか……」
lines.english: “Oh, right... You don’t own a computer...”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは眠たげな声で答えながら、ねむねむとまぶたのマッサージを始めました。どうやらけっこうお疲れで、ちょっと気を抜くと睡魔がやってくるみたいです。
lines.english: Yoneda answered in a sleepy voice and started rubbing her droopy eyelids. She looked pretty worn out; if she relaxed for even a second, she seemed ready to nod off.

lines.japanese: 「いやねー、要するに、ネットで鳳凰寺カケルを悪く言ってる連中ってのが結構いてさー」
lines.english: “Basically, quite a few people on the internet say nasty things about Kakeru Hououji.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「そう驚くことでもないでしょ。カケルって現場でもああだから、良く思ってない関係者なんて星の数ほどいるだろうし、プライベートじゃなおさら、ねえ？」
lines.english: “It isn’t so surprising. He acts like that on set too, so there must be countless people in the industry who dislike him. And in his private life, well...”

lines.japanese: 「や、ていうか、インターネットってそんななんすか」
lines.english: “Wait. Is that what the internet is like?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、漠然とした質問だね。そんなと言えばそんなだよ」
lines.english: “Hmm, that’s pretty vague. I guess you could say so.”

lines.japanese: 「うそーん、カルチャーショック。いやだわあ電脳社会」
lines.english: No waaay. Culture shock. Ugh, I hate the internet age.

lines.japanese: 「そういう一面もあるって話だよ。後学のためにも、ネットカフェとか行って見てみれば？」
lines.english: “That’s one side of it. Why not check out an internet café sometime, just for the experience?”

lines.japanese: 「ええー、やだ恐ーい、そんな見えない悪意の吹きだまりー。わたしダメなの、ひとの悪口とか言うのも聞くのも苦手なのー」
lines.english: Eww, no, scaaary. A whole cesspool of invisible malice. I can't handle it—I hate saying mean things about people, and I hate hearing them toooo.

lines.japanese: 俺がてのひらを頬に当ててくねくねしているうちに、米田さんはまたマウスをカチカチさせていました。
lines.english: While I pressed my palms to my cheeks and wriggled, Yoneda clicked the mouse again.

lines.japanese: 「ほら、こことか。雑誌の読者モデルとか追っかけてる娘たちが集まるサイトなんだけど、カケルってあのルックスでしょ、良くも悪くもその手の娘たちにチェックされやすいんだぁ」
lines.english: “Here, look. This site attracts girls who follow reader models from fashion magazines. With Kakeru's looks, they tend to keep tabs on him, for better or worse.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そっか、カケルくんたまに著者近影みたいな感じで顔出ししてますもんね」
lines.english: “Ah, right. Kakeru does occasionally show his face in one of those little author-photo boxes.”

lines.japanese: 「アレ、本人イヤがってるけどね。『いや俺はどうでもいいけどヨネに迷惑かかるかもよ』とか何とか言っちゃってさ。なーに迷惑って、おまえは指名手配でもされてんのか！　あはは！」
lines.english: “He hates that. He says things like, ‘I don’t care, but it could cause trouble for Yone.’ What trouble? Are you a wanted criminal? Ahaha!”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、そんで？　これは何なんすか？」
lines.english: “I see. So what is this?”

lines.japanese: 俺は米田さんの隣りに並んで、ディスプレイを覗きこんでみました。細かい文字の並んだ画面が、彼女の操作で下へ下へと流れていきます。
lines.english: I stood next to Yoneda and leaned in to look at the screen. With her scrolling, the rows of tiny text kept moving down and down.

lines.japanese: 「あのね、ここのＢＢＳはとくにカケルのアンチが多いの。笑っちゃうのが、たまに自称関係者だの自称元カノだの自称ナンパされただのが出没して──」
lines.english: “This particular BBS has a lot of Kakeru haters. The funny part is that every so often someone turns up claiming to be an insider, or an ex-girlfriend, or a woman he tried to pick up—”

lines.japanese: 「自称に優しい自称天国だ」
lines.english: “A paradise for anyone claiming to be anyone.”

lines.japanese: 「要は覆面座談会だからね、言ったもん勝ちだよ。わりと本物っぽいのが紛れてたりもするんだけど──」
lines.english: It's basically anonymous people talking, so whoever says it wins. Some of them do sound kinda real, though—

lines.japanese: 「──あ、この辺おもしろいよ。鳳凰寺カケル名言集。みんな、カケルのキャラよく掴んでるんだこれが」
lines.english: Oh, this part's funny. The Collected Sayings of Kakeru Hououji. And man, these people really get his character.

lines.japanese: 「え、読んで読んで」
lines.english: “Read them. Read them.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、じゃあこの辺から……」
lines.english: “All right, starting around here...”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは咳払いひとつしてから、カケルくんの声色と口調を真似て読みはじめました。
lines.english: Yoneda cleared her throat and began to read in an imitation of Kakeru’s voice and manner.

lines.japanese: 「『まあ、どんな容姿でも自信を持つことは大事だよね』」
lines.english: 'I mean, no matter what you look like, confidence is important.'

lines.japanese: 「うわ、言いそぉ……」
lines.english: “God, he would say that...”

lines.japanese: 「『ごめん、チョコは好きだけど君は嫌いだから』」
lines.english: “‘Sorry. I like chocolate, but I don’t like you.’”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、ホントっぽくて夢に見そぉ……」
lines.english: “That sounds real enough to haunt my dreams...”

lines.japanese: 「『死ねよ、腐れマ××』」
lines.english: “‘Die, you rotten c***.’”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、それも言いそうだぁ……ていうか、あああ、昨日聞いちゃったあああ」
lines.english: “He’d say that too... Wait, no! I heard him say it yesterday!”

lines.japanese: 「『あァ？　それ、俺の子だって証拠あんのかよ』」
lines.english: “‘The hell? Have you got proof the kid is mine?’”

lines.japanese: 「はは、それはまさか……いや、ビミョーか……絶対ないとも……」
lines.english: “Ha, surely not... Then again, I’m not so sure... I can’t say he absolutely wouldn’t...”

lines.japanese: 「『でも、そのひと最後は自分から腰振ってましたよ検事さん』」
lines.english: “‘But by the end, she was moving her hips herself, Mr. Prosecutor.’”

lines.japanese: 「ａｔ法廷！？」
lines.english: “At court?!”

lines.japanese: 「──まだまだあるけど、続ける？」
lines.english: “—There are plenty more. Want me to keep going?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、結構です……ぽんぽん痛くなってきました……あたたた」
lines.english: “No, thank you... My tummy is starting to hurt... Ow, ow.”

lines.japanese: 「あとね、街で見かけた鳳凰寺カケル、なんてスレもあって」
lines.english: Oh, and there's this thread called Kakeru Hououji Sightings...

lines.japanese: 「や、もういいですって」
lines.english: “I said that was enough.”

lines.japanese: 「深夜の雑木林からスコップ担いで出てきたとか、冬の波止場で人相の悪い男たちと中国語で密談していたとか、難病と闘う少年にホームランの約束をして勇気を与えていたとか」
lines.english: Like somebody saw him come out of some woods at midnight with a shovel over his shoulder, or whispering in Chinese with a bunch of scary-looking guys on a winter pier, or promising a home run to a boy fighting a serious illness to give him courage.

lines.japanese: 「も、ぜんぜん『街で』見かけてないじゃないすか。美談まぎれてるし」
lines.english: I mean, none of those are even sightings 'around town' anymore. And you slipped a heartwarming story in there.

lines.japanese: 「で実際カケルって、交遊関係どうなの？　なんか、ガラの悪い連中と一緒にいました系のタレコミ多いんだけど」
lines.english: So who does Kakeru actually hang around with? We keep getting tips that he's been seen with some pretty shady-looking guys.

lines.japanese: 「え、そうなんすか？」
lines.english: “Really?”

lines.japanese: 「あの子、いまはまだ写真週刊誌のネタになるほどの知名度ないけどさ。正直これからガンガン前に出ていける逸材だと思うんだよね。本人も作品もそういうオーラ出てるし」
lines.english: He's not famous enough for the tabloids to write about him yet, but honestly, I think he could really break out from here. He and his work both have that kind of presence.

lines.japanese: 「だから、あとはカケル自身がその辺マジメに考えてるかどうかなんだけど。私生活含めて」
lines.english: So it comes down to whether Kakeru himself is gonna take all that seriously. His private life too.

lines.japanese: 「あ、言っときますけど俺、カケルくんの私生活なんて知りませんよ。うちら暗黙の了解で、お互いのプライバシーに深く突っこまないすから」
lines.english: Just so you know, I don't know anything about Kakeru's private life. We've got this unspoken rule where we don't dig too deep into each other's business.

lines.japanese: 「なーんだ。キミら若いくせして、都会のマンションみたいな付き合いしてんだね」
lines.english: Aw, really? You guys are young, but you keep each other at arm's length like neighbors in some big-city apartment building.

lines.japanese: 「そそそ。こうね、深過ぎず浅過ぎずーぐらいが一番なんすよ、人間と人間は」
lines.english: Yeah, yeah, exactly. Not too deep, not too shallow—that's the sweet spot between people, y'know?

lines.japanese: 「はは～ん？　それは分かるけど、口に出来ちゃうのが若さよねえ鷲介クン？」
lines.english: “Oh, I understand the idea. But being able to say it aloud like that—that's youth for you, isn't it, Shusuke?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いまの発言、青かったすか」
lines.english: “Was that rather green of me?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっとねー。そんなことくれー、言われなくても大人はみんな知ってるのよ～ん♪」
lines.english: “A liiittle. Adults all know that much without being told, you kno-o-ow♪”

lines.japanese: 「ぅわお！　大人かっけぇー！」
lines.english: “Wow! Adults are so cool!”

lines.japanese: 「ああッ！　米田ァ、てめえこれ、また間違ってるじゃねえか！」
lines.english: “Ah! Yoneda, you bastard! This is wrong again!”
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 呑気な雑談に花を咲かせていると、とつぜん島端のお誕生席から悲鳴のような怒声が投げはなたれました。
lines.english: As our idle conversation blossomed, an anguished roar suddenly came flying from the desk at the head of the cluster.

lines.japanese: 「マップとキャプション、一個ずつズレてる！　先月と同じ間違い！」
lines.english: “Every map is offset by one caption! The same mistake as last month!”

lines.japanese: 青焼きの束を突きだし、それを残った手の甲でばしばし叩いてみせる壮年の編集者。米田さんは身を乗りだすように立ちあがりました。
lines.english: A middle-aged editor thrust out a sheaf of blue proofs and slapped them repeatedly with the back of his free hand. Yoneda surged to her feet.

lines.japanese: 「うぞっ！？」
lines.english: “No way!?”

lines.japanese: 「なんで俺が嘘つくんだよ！」
lines.english: “Why would I lie?”

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃあああ！　すいません至急修正します！」
lines.english: “Aaaah! I’m sorry! I’ll correct it immediately!”

lines.japanese: 両手で頭を抱えています。お、大人つれぇー。
lines.english: She clutched her head in both hands. Oof, being an adult was rough.

lines.japanese: 「えーと……それじゃ自分、そろそろ失礼しますね」
lines.english: “Well... I should probably be going.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あー、ごめんねえバタバタしちゃって。あはは、やーねーアイツ、ひとの細かいミスばっかり見つけちゃって。地図なんてちょっとぐらい間違えたって、ほっときゃ読者の方向音痴のせいになるのにねえ」
lines.english: Oh—uh, sorry, things got so hectic. Ahaha. Honestly, that guy's always picking at every tiny little mistake. A map can be a little off. Leave it alone and readers'll just think they've got no sense of direction.

lines.japanese: 「ないない、それはない」
lines.english: “No. Absolutely not.”

lines.japanese: 俺は最後にひとツッコミ入れてから、にこやかに頭を下げて出口へ向かいました。
lines.english: I got in one last jab, then gave her a cheerful bow and headed for the door.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、千歳君！　それじゃあ下の喫茶で時間潰しててよ。カケルのケータイに、そっちへ行くようメール入れとくから」
lines.english: “Oh, Chitose! Kill some time in the café downstairs. I’ll message Kakeru and tell him to meet you there.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それはどうも、お手数かけますー」
lines.english: “Thank you. Sorry for the trouble.”

lines.japanese: もう一度おじぎして、その後はすみやかに編集部を去りました。
lines.english: I bowed once more, then promptly left the editorial office.

lines.japanese: 入稿前の忙しい時期に、ちょっと長居しすぎちゃいましたかね。でも、渡すものだけ渡して帰るのもまた素っ気ないし。
lines.english: Maybe I'd hung around a little too long when they were this busy getting ready to go to press. But it'd also feel cold to just drop off what I came to deliver and leave.

lines.japanese: 引き際のタイミングって、いつでも難しいですよね？
lines.english: Finding the right moment to leave is always difficult, isn’t it?
